scenes.name: The question
scenes.intent: Open on the everyday magic: the phone knows where you are.

narration.text: Your phone always seems to know exactly where you are.
But how does it work out that little blue dot?

scenes.name: The satellites
scenes.intent: Reveal the constellation overhead that makes it possible.

narration.text: High above you, a fleet of GPS satellites circles the Earth.
At any moment, several of them are in view of your phone.

scenes.name: The signals
scenes.intent: Each satellite broadcasts; the signals race down to the phone.

narration.text: Each satellite constantly broadcasts the time and its position.
Those signals race down to your phone at the speed of light.

scenes.name: One distance
scenes.intent: Travel time becomes a distance -- a whole circle of possible spots.

narration.text: The signal's travel time tells the phone how far that satellite is.
That one distance places you somewhere on a circle around it.

scenes.name: Two distances
scenes.intent: A second circle cuts the possibilities down to two crossing points.

narration.text: Add a second satellite, and you get a second circle.
You must be standing where the two circles cross.

scenes.name: Three distances
scenes.intent: A third circle pins the location to a single point.

narration.text: A third satellite adds a third circle.
All three meet at exactly one point -- and that point is you.

scenes.name: The fix
scenes.intent: Zoom in on the meeting point the three distances agree on.

narration.text: The one place all three distances agree on is your location.
The phone settles on where the math meets.

scenes.name: The catch
scenes.intent: It all hinges on the clock: a tiny timing error is a huge distance error.

narration.text: But the whole trick rests on impeccably accurate clocks.
A billionth of a second off, and the distance is wrong by metres.

scenes.name: The fourth
scenes.intent: A fourth satellite solves the clock too; pull back on the finished fix.

narration.text: So a fourth satellite is added to solve for the clock as well.
Four numbers, one point -- and your phone knows exactly where you are.
